description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison of two sampling strategies—“Fine-to-Coarse Sampling Strategy” (purple bars) and “Uniform Sampling Strategy” (yellow bars)—across five values of the parameter *m* (6 through 10), measured by the metric MAP@10 on the vertical axis, which ranges from 23.0 to 27.0. For each value of *m*, two adjacent bars represent the respective strategies, with the purple bars consistently positioned to the left of the yellow bars within each *m* group. The Fine-to-Coarse strategy achieves higher MAP@10 scores across all *m* values: approximately 26.0 at *m*=6, peaking at ~26.8 at *m*=7, then slightly decreasing to ~26.3 at *m*=8, ~26.7 at *m*=9, and ~26.6 at *m*=10. In contrast, the Uniform strategy scores are lower, ranging from ~24.4 at *m*=6, rising to ~24.8 at *m*=7, peaking at ~25.6 at *m*=8, then declining to ~25.3 at *m*=9 and ~24.4 at *m*=10. The chart includes a legend in the upper right corner identifying the two strategies by color, and the horizontal axis is labeled “m” with integer tick marks from 6 to 10. Gridlines are present for easier value estimation, and the overall layout suggests a side-by-side comparison of performance trends as *m* increases.
